Legal Notes
===========

This project refers to third-party names, software products, and trademarks only in an informational and referential
context. Such references are used to describe compatibility, usage, or deployment targets, not to imply sponsorship,
endorsement, or affiliation.

Docker
------

Docker is a trademark of Docker, Inc. and is used here only to describe container images, build files, and runtime
commands. Any mention of Docker in this documentation or in generated artifacts is meant to identify the relevant
technology or command line tool, not to suggest that Docker, Inc. endorses this project.

When we write about Docker images, Dockerfiles, or Docker commands, we use the term in the ordinary technical sense.
We do not claim rights in the Docker mark and we do not use Docker logos or branding.

Linux
-----

Linux is used here as a referential name for the operating system and platform family. References to Linux in this
documentation are descriptive only and do not imply endorsement by Linus Torvalds, the Linux Foundation, or any
other rights holder.

Windows
-------

Windows is used here only to identify the operating system or platform that may run the tools described in this
project. Any mention of Windows is referential and does not imply endorsement, affiliation, or certification by
Microsoft.

Apple and macOS
---------------

Apple and macOS are used here only as referential product names when discussing Apple platforms or compatibility.
Their mention is descriptive and does not imply endorsement, sponsorship, or affiliation by Apple Inc.

Other Names
-----------

Other product names, package names, and trademarks mentioned in this documentation belong to their respective owners.
If such names appear in examples, they are used only as identifiers for the documented software or workflow.

This section is not legal advice. It is a short project-specific notice intended to make the documentation easier to
read and to keep the use of third-party marks explicit.
